content.text: {"concerns":[{"id":"SKP-001","concern":"Hash-chain recovery via git history is unreliable for untracked logs and creates a recoverable-by-design illusion. §3.4.4 says 'Attempt rebuild from git history' but §3.7 declares L1/L2/L3/L5 audit logs UNTRACKED. Untracked files have no git history to rebuild from, so the recovery path silently fails for the majority of audit logs. The weekly snapshot job creates a 7-day RPO gap acknowledged in §3.7 but not reconciled with §3.4.4's recovery procedure.","severity":"CRITICAL","severity_score":860,"why_matters":"The audit substrate is the project's primary safety claim (G-2: 'zero unaudited dispatches'). A chain break in .run/panel-decisions.jsonl or .run/cost-budget-events.jsonl between weekly snapshots is unrecoverable, yet §3.4.4 implies recovery is generally possible. Operators will trust the recovery procedure based on the SDD, then discover at incident time that 7 days of L1/L2 history is gone. This undermines non-repudiation and forensic review for the most safety-critical primitives (panel decisions, budget verdicts).","location":"§3.4.4 Hash-Chain Recovery vs §3.7 Persistence policy table; L1/L2/L3/L5 logs marked UNTRACKED","recommendation":"Reconcile §3.4.4 with §3.7 explicitly: state that git-history rebuild only applies to TRACKED logs (L4 trust-ledger, handoffs, trust-store). For UNTRACKED chain-integrity-required logs, document recovery as snapshot-restore with explicit unrecoverable gap, the [GAP-RESTORED-FROM-SNAPSHOT] marker semantics, and the RPO=7d limitation as a Sprint 1 acceptance criterion. Consider reducing snapshot cadence to daily for L1/L2 or making L1/L2 logs TRACKED with redaction."},{"id":"SKP-002","concern":"Sprint 1 is severely overloaded and contains the cycle's entire shared infrastructure plus L1 plus 7+ new acceptance criteria added in v1.4. The Sprint 1 deliverables list spans 12 cross-cutting items (audit envelope, JCS adapters in 3 languages with conformance vectors, sanitize_for_session_start, tier-validator, protected-class registry, operator-identity, lore directory, status integration, baseline instrumentation, retention compaction, hash-chain recovery, audit-keys bootstrap) plus L1's 9 ACs plus IMP-003 bootstrap criteria plus SKP-004 benchmark plus SKP-007 decision. The 'Week 1-1.5' estimate is implausible.","severity":"HIGH","severity_score":780,"why_matters":"Sprint 1 sets the schema versions, signing scheme, canonicalization library, and bootstrap flow that all subsequent sprints depend on. If Sprint 1 slips or ships incomplete, every later sprint inherits the slip plus integration debt. R11 acknowledges 6-10 week timeline risk, but Sprint 4.5 buffer doesn't help when the bottleneck is at Sprint 1. The de-scope triggers ('any sprint >2× planned') will fire on Sprint 1 first, with no fallback because the cross-cutting items are not optional.","location":"§8 Sprint 1: L1 + Cross-Cutting Infrastructure (Week 1-1.5)","recommendation":"Split Sprint 1 into Sprint 0 (cross-cutting infrastructure only — envelope, JCS, signing, bootstrap, tier-validator, protected-class, operator-identity) and Sprint 1 (L1 only, building on Sprint 0). Re-baseline timeline to 7-11 weeks. Alternatively, defer JCS multi-language conformance vectors to the sprint that first needs cross-language verification (likely Sprint 4 or 7), shipping bash-only JCS in Sprint 1."},{"id":"SKP-003","concern":"Tool-call boundary policy (§1.9.3.2 Layer 5) depends on a heuristic 'any tool call within first N turns where SessionStart content was present' to identify untrusted-provenance frames. N is unspecified, the heuristic is brittle (multi-turn conditioning attacks defeat first-N-turn windows), and there is no mechanism for the agent to clear or extend the untrusted-provenance taint. The provenance is also stored 'in conversation metadata, not in user-message body' but Loa's existing architecture for conversation metadata propagation across tool calls is not documented or referenced.","severity":"HIGH","severity_score":740,"why_matters":"The hard tool-call boundary is the v1.2 mitigation for SKP-002 prompt-injection (CRITICAL 890). If the provenance taint is clearable by waiting N+1 turns, or if the metadata mechanism doesn't actually exist in Loa's harness, the entire defense-in-depth claim collapses to Layer 1-3 framing — which the SDD itself characterizes as insufficient. The 'honest caveat' at the end of §1.9.3.2 acknowledges this depends on the harness routing tool calls through the resolver, but does not validate that conversation metadata actually flows through the harness intact.","location":"§1.9.3.2 Layer 5 — Hard tool-call boundary","recommendation":"Specify N concretely (or replace with a session-scoped or content-bound provenance model where the taint persists until SessionStart content is explicitly dismissed by operator action). Cite the specific Loa harness component that propagates conversation metadata across tool calls, or ship that propagation as a Sprint 1 cross-cutting deliverable. Add a Sprint 7 jailbreak corpus test specifically for multi-turn conditioning attacks that wait out the N-turn window."},{"id":"S
